title: Tarrasch Variation (3.Nd2)
intro: White plays 3.Nd2 to avoid the ...Bb4 pin. Strike at once with 3...c5, develop actively against the isolated pawn, or play 4...Qxd5 against Ngf3.

lessons.title: The Open Tarrasch (3...c5)
lessons.summary: Strike with 3...c5 and develop active pieces around the d5 pawn.

steps.text: With 3.Nd2, White defends e4 while keeping c3 free for a pawn. However, the knight on d2 blocks the c1 bishop and puts no pressure on d5.

steps.hint: Strike at d4 with your c-pawn.
steps.ifRight: Black fights for the centre at once.

steps.text: Take back to get open lines for both bishops, even if d5 becomes isolated.
steps.hint: Capture on d5 with the e-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...exd5: your pieces will develop rapidly to active squares.
steps.ifRight: Now your c8 bishop is completely free.

feedback.d8d5: 4...Qxd5 is playable too, though 4...exd5 gives Black rapid, easy piece play.

steps.text: Develop your queen's knight and control d4 and e5.
White pins the knight with 6.Bb5. Develop your dark-squared bishop actively.
steps.hint: Put the f8 bishop on d6, eyeing the kingside.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...Bd6: if White plays 7.dxc5, 7...Bxc5 develops cleanly.
steps.ifRight: Black develops ...Nge7 and ...O-O next with active pieces.

lessons.title: Meeting 4.Ngf3 and 4.c3
lessons.summary: Trade on d4 and keep a healthy pawn structure with ...Qxd5.

steps.text: Instead of taking on d5 at once, White often plays 4.Ngf3.
Clear the central tension before White develops further.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...cxd4: if White takes 5.exd5, you recapture cleanly with the queen.
steps.ifRight: White must choose how to recapture.

steps.text: Recapture with the queen so you keep a healthy pawn structure.
steps.hint: Take on d5 with your queen.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Qxd5: after 6.Bc4 Qd6 (or 6...Qd8), your pawns stay intact.
steps.ifRight: Black avoids an isolated pawn and develops ...Nf6 and ...Nc6 smoothly.

steps.text: What if White supports d4 with 4.c3?
steps.hint: Take on d4 so White must recapture with the c-pawn, or develop ...Nc6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...cxd4 (or 4...Nc6): after 5.cxd4 dxe4 6.Nxe4, Black gets easy play with ...Nc6 and ...Nf6.
steps.ifRight: White's d4 pawn becomes an easy target.

steps.text: If White captures 5.Nxd4 after 4...cxd4, develop and challenge the centre.
steps.hint: Develop your queen's knight to c6 or king's knight to f6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Nc6 (or 5...Nf6) to fight for e5 and d4.
steps.ifRight: Black develops rapidly with ...Nf6 and ...Be7 or ...Bc5.

lessons.title: Playing with the isolated d5 pawn
lessons.summary: Put the knight on e7, save the bishop on b6, and castle.

steps.text: In the isolated pawn position, Black's d5 pawn gives extra space and open lines for the pieces. Develop quickly and watch out for Nb3.
Develop your king's knight without inviting a Bg5 pin.
steps.hint: Put the g8 knight on e7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8...Nge7 so you avoid a pin after Bg5 and prepare ...O-O.
steps.ifRight: The knight sits nicely on e7 and leaves ...Bg4 free.

feedback.g8f6: 8...Nf6 is playable too, though 8...Nge7 avoids 9.Bg5 pins cleanly.

steps.text: White chases your active c5 bishop with 9.Nb3.
Keep the bishop on its strong kingside diagonal.
steps.hint: Step back one square to b6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9...Bb6 so the bishop keeps aiming at f2 and stays safe.
steps.ifRight: The bishop stays active on b6.
Black is castled with active bishops and plans ...Bg4 or ...Qd6.
